title: 18 November
subtitle: A special day in BAPS history
headline: Prime Minister of Canada, Rt. Hon. Stephen Harper, Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi , India
story:
On Wednesday 18 November 2009, the Prime Minster of Canada, Right Honorable Stephen Harper, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi to experience India’s art, culture and values. On behalf of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the inspirer and creator of Swaminarayan Akshardham and Spiritual Head of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, BAPS International Convenor, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, welcomed the Prime Minister in traditional manner by applying a chandlo to his forehead, tying a nada chhadi to his wrist and placing a sanctified flower garland around his neck in a gesture of peace and friendship.

Feeling he was transported back in time, Prime Minster Harper expressed, “I just can’t believe this temple was created in modern times. It’s amazing how ancient this temple looks.” During his one hour visit, the Prime Minster admired the Mayur Dwar (Peacock Gate) and the Gajendra Pithika (Elephant Plinth).

Marveling at the beautifully carved stone elephants, Prime Minister Harper called upon Hon. Lawrence Cannon, Minister of Foreign Affairs, and other in the delegation to note the intricately carved stone texture of the elephants which seemed so realistic. The Prime Minster offered prayers for world peace and harmony and for the strengthening of Indo-Canadian relationships by offering ‘abhishek’, the ceremonial pouring of sacred water from 151 holy rivers, lakes and ponds across India, on the sacred image of Neelkanth Varni.

Thereafter, the Prime Minister sat in the Sanskruti Vihar boat ride exhibition displaying 10,000 years of India’s glorious heritage. Expressing his experience in the guest opinion book, the Prime Minister wrote: “This is an extraordinary place. It is just overwhelming.

I cannot express it with words. I hope I will be able to return and see it all in far greater detail.” Before departing, the Prime MInister conveyed his gratitude to HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj, “Thank His Holiness for gifting a beautiful temple to Canada and I deeply value his blessings for peace for he is a man of great peace and travels everywhere to spread that peace.” The Canadian delegation accompanying the Prime Minister included Hon.

Lawrence Cannon, Minister of Foreign Affairs, five Members of Parliament: Deepak Obhrai, Nina Grewal, Patrick Brown, Devinder Shory and Tim Uppal, High Commissioners of both India and Canada, and leading Canadian businessmen of Indian origin.

options.headline: Murti-pratishtha rituals of deities for hari mandirs in the villages of Nana Rajkot and Ugamedi
options.story:
The murti-pratishtha rituals of deities for hari mandirs in the villages of Nana Rajkot and Ugamedi were carried out during Swamishri’s morning puja. Thereafter Swamishri performed pujan and arti of the deities.

Performs murti-pratishtha rituals of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and deities for hari mandirs in Ugamedi and Nana Rajkot. Performs pradakshina at the Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir with bhaktas in a joyful mood. Blesses and advices the bhaktas during samip darshan. Blesses the satsang assembly. Is welcomed with a garland. Doing darshan and pradakshina at the holy shrine in the mandir grounds. Meets bhaktas in the mandir pradakshina. Performs his morning puja on the grounds of Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir. Doing darshan at the old Swaminarayan Mandir. Descends the mandir steps. Bapa with students having graduated in 10th grade from Pramukh Swami Vidya Mandir (school) in Sarangpur. Blesses a baby bull, Rudranath, of the mandir gaushala. Meets Haka Khachar and bhaktas. BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Gadhada. Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Shri Gopinath Dev. Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami and Shri Gopalanand Swami. Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj. Doing darshan of holy relics of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Darshan of charnarvind at the old Mandir. Doing darshan of Shri Vaasudevnarayan's orda in Dada Khachar's darbar. Doing Thakorji's darshan. Shri Varninath and Shri Gopinath Dev. Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj. Morning puja at Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir.

Prime Minister of Canada, Rt. Hon. Stephen Harper,
Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi , India
lines: Prime Minister of Canada, Rt. Hon. Stephen Harper,
Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi , India

items.text:
On Wednesday 18 November 2009, the Prime Minster of Canada, Right Honorable Stephen Harper, visited Swaminarayan
Akshardham in New Delhi to experience India’s art, culture and values. On behalf of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the
inspirer and creator of Swaminarayan Akshardham and Spiritual Head of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, BAPS International
Convenor, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, welcomed the Prime Minister in traditional manner by applying a chandlo to his forehead,
tying a nada chhadi to his wrist and placing a sanctified flower garland around his neck in a gesture of peace and friendship.

Feeling he was transported back in time, Prime Minster Harper expressed, “I just can’t believe this temple was created in modern times. It’s amazing how
ancient this temple looks.” During his one hour visit, the Prime Minster admired the Mayur Dwar (Peacock Gate) and the Gajendra Pithika (Elephant Plinth).

Marveling at the beautifully carved stone elephants, Prime Minister Harper called upon Hon. Lawrence Cannon, Minister of Foreign
Affairs, and other in the delegation to note the intricately carved stone texture of the elephants which seemed so realistic. The Prime
Minster offered prayers for world peace and harmony and for the strengthening of Indo-Canadian relationships by offering ‘abhishek’,
the ceremonial pouring of sacred water from 151 holy rivers, lakes and ponds across India, on the sacred image of Neelkanth Varni.

Thereafter, the Prime Minister sat in the Sanskruti Vihar boat ride exhibition displaying 10,000 years of India’s glorious heritage.
Expressing his experience in the guest opinion book, the Prime Minister wrote: “This is an extraordinary place. It is just overwhelming.

I cannot express it with words. I hope I will be able to return and see it all in far greater detail.” Before departing, the Prime MInister conveyed his
gratitude to HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj, “Thank His Holiness for gifting a beautiful temple to Canada and I deeply value his blessings for peace
for he is a man of great peace and travels everywhere to spread that peace.” The Canadian delegation accompanying the Prime Minister included Hon.

Lawrence Cannon, Minister of Foreign Affairs, five Members of Parliament: Deepak Obhrai, Nina Grewal, Patrick Brown, Devinder
Shory and Tim Uppal, High Commissioners of both India and Canada, and leading Canadian businessmen of Indian origin.
